name: Pace Digitek Ltd
title: Pace Digitek Ltd - 544550 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Pace Digitek Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 60.5% YoY to Rs.1,097 crore; FY26 PAT Rs.307 crore (+10.1%), FY27 revenue guided Rs.3,200-3,400 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs.1,097 crore versus Rs.683 crore a year earlier, driven by project execution. Full-year revenue grew 8.3% to Rs.2,641 crore and PAT rose 10.1% to Rs.307 crore, but full-year EBITDA fell to Rs.455 crore from Rs.482 crore as the mix shifted from telecom to energy. Working capital absorbed cash: inventory was built to Rs.540 crore and trade receivables reached Rs.2,442 crore, which management expects to ease by September 2026. BESS manufacturing capacity is being raised from 2.5 GWh to 5 GWh (July 2026) and 10 GWh (October 2026).

segments.name: Energy (BESS, BOO, EPC)
segments.commentary: Energy is 78.1% of the Rs.11,338 crore executable order book (Rs.8,854 crore) and 45% of FY26 revenue. Energy EBITDA margins are currently below telecom margins; 2.5 GWh plant ran at about 80% utilisation in FY26, delivering 178 containers and 480 MWh of utility-scale execution.

segments.name: Telecom & ICT
segments.commentary: Telecom & ICT is 21.9% of the order book (Rs.2,484 crore) and contributed 55% of FY26 revenue. Recent wins include further BSNL and Railways orders, a RailTel order for Railway Kavach infrastructure (tickets Rs.100-250 crore), and CCTV on coaches.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at Rs.3,200-3,400 crore; FY28 at Rs.4,000-4,200 crore (top line reported net of intra-company transactions).
FY27 PAT margin expected at 10-11%, down from 11.4% in FY26, as lower-margin energy orders rise in the mix.
BOO projects expected to contribute 20-25% of FY27 revenue (about Rs.800-1,000 crore) and about Rs.1,000 crore in FY28; BOO PAT margin targeted around 10%.
Cash flow from operations expected to normalise by September 2026; management said FY28 would be CFO positive.
Cell price rise of about 20% from 1 April 2026 expected to ease from the next quarter; bids include contingency for input cost increases.
African channel with NEC XON: 300-500 MWh of orders expected in FY27, growing 20-25% in FY28.
In-house container fabrication expected to improve pricing and operating efficiency by about 4-5%.
capex_capacity: BESS manufacturing at 2.5 GWh operational in FY26 with about 80% utilisation; target is about 80% utilisation by end of FY27 once 10 GWh is running.
5 GWh expansion: machinery received from China, installation underway, operational from July 2026 (delayed about two months by West Asia shipping disruption).
5 GWh second line ordered, expected operational October 2026, taking total to 10 GWh; plant and infrastructure for a further expansion to 10 GWh already built.
In-house container fabrication plant ready, operational from July 2026.
Open order book about 5.32 GWh, of which 2.72 GWh is BOO; MSEDCL BOO project expected to generate about Rs.1,000 crore revenue in FY27.
Cell manufacturing is under consideration; an announcement is expected soon.
demand_pricing: Current container realisation is about $82-84/kWh versus cell cost of $48-50/kWh; cells are about 60-65% of container cost.
Cell prices rose about 20% from 1 April 2026 due to regulatory changes (China export rebate cut from 9% to 6%); the company used stocked cells bought at earlier prices to protect Q1 FY27 margins.
Government BESS tenders are won on L1 basis; private customers weigh manufacturing, field operations and support. First non-captive customer L&T placed a 250 MWh order in January 2026.
C&I BESS (kWh scale) is a new focus; state policies in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Rajasthan mandate BESS with solar of 50 MW and above.
Management said competition will rise; the company claims about 6 GWh open order book and first commissioned project (September 2025) as operating credential.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capacity commissioning delay a bottleneck, and are imports from China affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the delay was two months, caused by West Asia shipping disruption; equipment has arrived and will be commissioned in June and operational from July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current cell cost and expected pass-through, and what are container realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Container realisation is about $82-84/kWh and cell cost $48-50/kWh (60-65% of container cost); management expects prices to ease from the next quarter and is not delaying projects currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 margins hold given energy is the bulk of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Energy EBITDA margins are lower than telecom; PAT margin is expected to be 10-11% in FY27 versus 11.4% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why do FY25 receivables differ from the RHP figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs.295 crore (FY26) and Rs.1,271 crore (FY25) were regrouped as non-current receivables, mainly a BSNL five-year milestone schedule; analyst still reported a gap and was asked to email for clarification.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics of the MSEDCL BOO project?
qa_highlights.answer: Project cost about Rs.1.2 crore/MWh ex-GST, reduced to about Rs.93 lakh/MWh after VGF of about Rs.27 lakh/MWh; government pays Rs.2,19,000 per MW per month; SPV-level IRR about 12-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was working capital stretched and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was built ahead of cell price rises; Q4 sales of Rs.1,097 crore created receivables on 90-120 day cycles. Rs.300 crore was collected in April-May and receivables are expected to ease by September 2026.

risks_watch: Input cost risk: cell prices up about 20% from 1 April 2026; if elevated prices persist, project timelines and margins may be hit, and force majeure provisions may be invoked.
Receivables of Rs.2,442 crore and working capital strain; watch for collections by September 2026 and CFO turning positive.
Margin dilution as energy (lower margin) rises in revenue mix; FY27 PAT margin guided lower at 10-11%.
Execution risk on 5 GWh (July 2026) and 10 GWh (October 2026) capacity ramp, and on reaching ~80% utilisation by end FY27.
Reporting questions on receivables reclassification (Rs.295 crore non-current, Rs.1,271 crore FY25) were not fully resolved on the call.
Funding: no equity or warrant raise planned; BOO projects paused beyond the fourth project unless external investment is secured.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book, capacity expansion and FY27-28 guidance, but defensive and somewhat evasive on the receivables reclassification question and on the detailed cell cost impact, which was answered only in broad terms.
key_quotes: We have also successfully executed 480 megawatt hours (MWh) of utility-scale BESS capacity during FY26.
By October, we would have a 10 GWh of operational capacity.
Cell costs account for ~ 60% of overall BESS system value.
Energy EBITDA margins are lower than telecom.
